newsitem.title: POLAND: Bankwatch upgrades Slaski to IC-B rating.
newsitem.headline: Bankwatch upgrades Slaski to IC-B rating.

text.p: Thomson BankWatch increased its rating for Poland's Bank Slaski SA as a domestic issuer to IC-B, the bank said in a statement on Friday.
Slaski did not give the previous rating and no one at the bank was immediately available for comment.
Bankwatch also maintained its LC-1 short-term local currency rating for Slaski, the statement said.

It said Bankwatch lifted its domestic issuer rating after Dutch ING Bank had upped its stake in Slaski last June to 54.08 from 25.9 percent. The bank became the first of the nine carved out of the central bank to become foreign owned.

"We think Bank Slaski SA, which is already an innovative bank adapting to Western standards, will strengthen its competitive position in the future as a result of its further tightening its links with ING," the statement quoted Bankwatch.
It noted Slaski's planned upgrading of its computer system this year, which should help diversify retail banking services.

Bankwatch said Slaski was more profitable than most banks in the region even though it had more bad debts than most, because Slaski, unlike most regional banks, had not received government restructuring bonds.
Instead, Slaski formed reserves from its own funds, which lowered its capital ratio in comparison to similar banks.
